problem: Consider the arc of the curve $y=\frac{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}}{2}$ that lies between the lines $x=0$ and $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡2.$ Calculate the surface area generated when this arc is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi y\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since we're given a curve in the form $y=f(x),$ we have 

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}y\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${x}_{1}=0$ to ${x}_{2}=\operatorname{ln}⁡2.$ 

Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}}{2})=\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{2}\,⇒\,{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}=\frac{{({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})}^{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}y\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(\frac{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}}{2})\sqrt{1+\frac{{({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})}^{2}}{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(\frac{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}}{2})\sqrt{\frac{4+{e}^{2x}-2+{e}^{-2x}}{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x})\sqrt{{e}^{2x}+2+{e}^{-2x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x})\sqrt{{({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x})}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({e}^{2x}+2+{e}^{-2x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2x}+2x-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2x}]}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}(\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2})-\frac{\pi }{2}(\frac{1}{2}{e}^{0}+2(0)-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-0}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}(\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4+2\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\pi (1+\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{(15+16\operatorname{ln}⁡2)\pi }{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
